title: Decision: coordinated merge workflow for parallel PRs touching shared structs
description:
## Decision

When opening 3+ PRs that touch the same files, use fast sequential merge with pre-resolution: plan merge order upfront, keep worktrees alive, and proactively resolve conflicts after each merge before moving to the next.

## Rationale

PRs #92-95 all added fields to the same structs (Config, ReloadedConfig, DeployConfig, ConfigFromEnv). Merging them sequentially caused cascading conflicts — PR #95 needed three rounds of conflict resolution as each prior merge shifted the base. The conflicts were all mechanical (additive struct fields, keep-both-sides) but time-consuming. Keeping specs separate was correct — review quality and independent rollback are worth the merge pain.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Spec as one change**: Avoids conflicts but creates 1500+ line PRs, defeats independent review, couples unrelated rollback. Rejected.
- **Stacked PRs** (each branch based on previous): Eliminates conflicts but creates rigid merge order. If PR #2 needs changes, #3-4 all need rebasing. Too fragile.
- **Umbrella integration branch**: Merge all into staging, resolve once, merge staging to main. Clean but adds process overhead and a branch to maintain. Overkill for 3-4 PRs.

## Workflow

1. Plan merge order upfront (broadest shared surface first)
2. Keep worktrees alive until all PRs are merged
3. After each merge, immediately pull main into remaining worktrees and resolve
4. Don't wait for CodeRabbit between merges — batch conflict resolution while context is hot

## Future Mitigation

- bosun-j1c (ConfigField[T]) will reduce shared surface — new reloadable fields won't need FromEnv booleans or reload guard conditions
- bosun-eln (reconcile split) will reduce file-level conflicts by splitting the 2200-line files
close_reason: Decision recorded — workflow captured for future parallel PR merges

title: Image update policy: auto vs pinned per-service
description: Add per-service image update policy so Bosun can own both config AND image updates. Two strategies: (1) pinned — Bosun deploys exactly what Git declares, updates only on version bump commits. (2) auto — Bosun runs docker compose pull before compose up for services tagged auto, pulling mutable tags like :latest. This replaces Watchtower for Bosun-managed services and closes the gap where two update mechanisms (Watchtower + Bosun) don't know about each other. title: Architectural ceiling: drift detection is Docker-local only

Breaking this requires DockerClientFunc to support remote Docker endpoints (DOCKER_HOST, Docker-over-SSH, TLS). See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

title: Refactor reloadable config: replace *FromEnv booleans with ConfigField[T] source-tracking pattern

Each reloadable field requires wiring in ConfigFromEnv, reloadProjectConfig, and tests. The 'has anything changed' guard on line 745 grows with every new field. Replace with a ConfigField[T] generic that tracks source (env/file/default) and handles precedence internally. Depends on bosun-eln (reconcile split) landing first to avoid a 2200-line merge.

On startup or trigger, compare against this rather than just git diff. This catches interrupted deployments and automatically re-runs them.

title: Architectural ceiling: webhook handler is GitHub-only

GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo, and Bitbucket must use the generic /webhook endpoint with no signature validation and no branch filtering. Common for homelabs running self-hosted Gitea/Forgejo. Breaking this requires a WebhookProvider interface with Verify() and ParsePush() methods, a provider registry, and route registration driven by config. See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

title: Architectural ceiling: single-target reconciler
description: The reconciler is structurally limited to one target per instance. Config has one TargetHost, one StateFile, one StagingDir, one ProjectName. The daemon holds one Reconciler. Multi-server ('one yacht, many ports') requires running N separate daemon processes with no coordination. Related sub-ceilings: (1) state file is process-local, (2) single shared staging directory prevents concurrent reconciles, (3) secrets are flat-merged with no per-target scoping. Breaking this requires Config becoming a list of target descriptors, per-target state files, per-run staging directories, and namespaced secrets. See docs/gitops-comparison.md.
